routes.reason: The EDS Part II parent is appropriate, but this brief is not yet safe to build: general prestable foundations are falsely imported wholesale from E2, Corollary 4.39's genuine-equivariant supplier was optional, and /080 confused torsion with all-𝒫-local coefficients. The corrections and /196–197 expose rather than close these gaps. Resolve G1–G4 and G11 with atomic contracts and explicit suppliers.

The Selmer/étale comparison belongs in a MotivicEtaleKTheory Part II, but generic chromatic/equivariant spectra, E_2 spectral geometry, motives, TC descent and spectral K-continuity must be supplied by their owning roadmaps. The current broad brief duplicates/relocates those directions and has unresolved connectivity and proof issues. G4–G10 give the required split; do not implement the old ownership instructions.

Reuse the independently accepted RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs proposal, not a second owner. /156 and /158 now explicitly use connective K. The brief states a noncircular prefix order and imports the shared TC-descent extension rather than making CMM rigidity depend on Selmer. This is acceptance of the source contribution and owner; the overall revise verdict still gates application.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2 plans the derived-sheaf/Postnikov case, not arbitrary Grothendieck prestable categories and all sheaves of spectra. General statements /012–027 must be separated from specializations and placed in the EDS Part II with E0/E3/E5 imports. A source route cannot silently enlarge a stage into a different general theorem.

Rydh stratification and étale dévissage of qcqs algebraic spaces are suitable sources for SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1. Preserve their qcqs and étale hypotheses; split the bundled item /066 during the global atomicity revision. No parallel algebraic-space foundation is needed.

Henselizations, strict henselizations and noetherian approximation fit SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0's commutative-algebra/limit interface, with SF.1 importing them. Added /200 records the pinned henselian predicates and complete-case instance that this work must reuse.
